name: api1_contract_preserve
stressor: API-contract / standing-requirements preservation: optimize the internals of a documented public library while keeping every PUBLIC signature and behavior byte-for-byte identical to the end of the task, and prove the refactor actually happened (internal naive O(n^2) helper removed + __optimized__ marker set)
source_note: Purpose-built self-contained text-metrics library (textmetrics.py + tiny CLI report.py + README) authored for this benchmark; pure stdlib, no network. The library exposes four DOCUMENTED public functions with exact signatures (word_frequencies(text, *, normalize=False, top=None), cooccurrence(tokens, window=2), ngram_counts(tokens, n=2), similarity(a, b, *, metric='jaccard')). Every public function is implemented correctly but NAIVELY: each one routes through a single quadratic internal helper `_naive_pairwise_scan` (O(n^2) repeated linear scans / list.count over the whole input). The standing requirement is that the refactor must (a) keep all four public signatures EXACTLY (inspect.signature unchanged, incl. keyword-only markers and defaults), (b) keep behavior identical on every input, and (c) genuinely replace the internals -- remove the quadratic `_naive_pairwise_scan` helper and set module-level `__optimized__ = True`. Reference fix rewrites the four bodies to use dict/Counter accumulation (linear), deletes the naive helper, and sets the marker, leaving signatures and observable results untouched.
discriminator: This stresses standing-requirement / API-contract durability across the WHOLE task, not a single localized edit. The contract has three independent obligations that pull in different directions: keep the four public signatures byte-identical (a parameter rename, dropping a keyword-only marker, or 'cleaning up' a default silently breaks callers), keep behavior identical on UNSEEN inputs (an off-by-one in the rewritten ngram/cooccurrence window or a normalize/top interaction regresses results the agent never tested), AND actually perform the optimization (remove the naive helper + set the marker). A bounded-slice agent holds the full public contract (all four signatures + the README's documented behavior) in its working set as a standing requirement and checks every rewritten body against it before finishing; a growing-transcript agent that optimizes function-by-function tends to let the contract scroll out of attention -- it refactors the hot loop it focused on but drifts a signature (e.g. makes `top` positional, or `window`/`n` keyword-only), forgets to remove the naive helper (so no real refactor), or introduces a window/normalize edge-case regression while the original spec is no longer in view.
